def factor_cycle_return_skewness(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    skew = ret.rolling(120, min_periods=60).skew()
    df_copy["factor_cycle_return_skewness"] = skew
    return df_copy["factor_cycle_return_skewness"]
description: Return distribution asymmetry is a well-documented cyclical feature. Early bull phases often exhibit positive skewness as upside surprises dominate, while late bull and bear phases exhibit negative skewness as downside shocks become more frequent. A 120-day rolling skewness of daily returns captures this slow-moving cyclical state transition. Unlike volatility ratios or moving-average crosses, skewness measures the shape of the return distribution, providing an orthogonal view of market-phase evolution. The raw signal is stock-specific and becomes more negative as downside tail risk increases, useful for ranking cross-sectionally after neutralization.
